deep.reconstruction:
This page is Art. 10 of Riemann's Inaugural Dissertation (Göttingen 1851, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'). It appears to be a draft or fair copy of that article. It applies the integral theorem of Art. 9 to harmonic functions to obtain Green's representation formula and the mean-value property. Notation: p is the normal to the boundary, pointing into T (Riemann's convention). Art. 9 states ∫(X ∂x/∂p + Y ∂y/∂p) ds = -∫∫(∂X/∂x + ∂Y/∂y) dT.

(1) Green's second identity. Take X = u u'_x - u' u_x and Y = u u'_y - u' u_y. Then X_x + Y_y = u Δu' - u' Δu, because the cross terms u_x u'_x cancel. So if Δu = Δu' = 0, the field (X, Y) is divergence-free. The boundary integral ∫(X x_p + Y y_p) ds equals ∫(u ∂u'/∂p - u' ∂u/∂p) ds, and the theorems of Art. 9 apply to it.

(2) Isolated singularities are negligible. Hypotheses on u:
- the discontinuities of u and of its first derivatives do not fill a line;
- at each discontinuity point, ρ u_x → 0 and ρ u_y → 0 as ρ → 0, where ρ is the distance of the variable point O from that point.

Under these, the singularities can be ignored by the Remark to III of Art. 9. That remark requires ρX → 0 and ρY → 0 at the singular point. Proof:
- Along each ray from the singular point, ρ ∂u/∂ρ = ρ(u_x x_ρ + u_y y_ρ) stays bounded for ρ < R.
- Let U = u(R), and let 𝔘 = sup |ρ u_ρ| on (0, R).
- Integrating u_ρ (bound ≤ 𝔘/ρ) from ρ to R gives |u - U| ≤ 𝔘 |log ρ - log R|.
- Hence ρ(u - U) → 0, since ρ log ρ → 0, and therefore ρu → 0.
- With u' regular, it follows that ρX → 0 and ρY → 0, so the case of Art. 9 applies.

(3) Fundamental solution. Assume T is schlicht, i.e. lies simply over the plane A. Fix O_0 = (x_0, y_0) with u(O_0) = u_0. Then log r = ½ log((x - x_0)² + (y - y_0)²) satisfies Δ log r = 0 and is singular only at O_0.

(4) Put u' = log r. By Art. 9 III, the integral ∫(u ∂log r/∂p - log r ∂u/∂p) ds over the whole boundary of T equals the same integral over any small curve around O_0. Choose a circle r = const, parametrised by the angle φ. There ∂/∂p = -∂/∂r (my reading of the orientation) and ds = r dφ. The integral becomes
-∫_0^{2π} u (∂log r/∂r) r dφ - log r ∫ (∂u/∂p) ds.
The flux ∫ (∂u/∂p) ds vanishes (Art. 9 with u' = 1), so the integral equals -∫_0^{2π} u dφ.

(5) On the next page this tends to -2π u_0 as r → 0. Hence
u_0 = (1/2π) ∫(log r ∂u/∂p - u ∂log r/∂p) ds   (Green's representation formula)
u_0 = (1/2π) ∫_0^{2π} u dφ   (mean-value property).
The next page then uses these to prove the regularity / removable-singularity theorem.
errors: The inequality u - U < 𝔘(log ρ - log R) is stated 'abgesehen vom Zeichen'. Literally the right side is negative for ρ < R, so it must be read with absolute values: |u - U| ≤ 𝔘 |log ρ - log R|. Riemann signals this himself ('in derselben Bedeutung genommen').

R is chosen ray by ray. Applying the Remark to III over small circles needs ρu → 0 uniformly in direction. This follows from the hypothesis if ρ u_x, ρ u_y → 0 uniformly, which is implicit but not stated. This is a minor rigor gap typical of the period.
Using ∫(∂u/∂p) ds = 0 on the circle presupposes that the same singularity-removal argument applies with u' = 1. This is fine but left implicit.

results.what: u Δu' - u' Δu = div(u ∇u' - u' ∇u), and the resulting boundary identity for harmonic u, u'
Isolated singularities at which ρ|∇u| → 0 do not affect the integral theorems, since ρu → 0 via the bound |u - U| ≤ C|log ρ|
results.modern_name: Removable singularity condition for harmonic functions (growth o(1/ρ) of the gradient)

results.what: u(O_0) = (1/2π) ∮(log r ∂u/∂n - u ∂log r/∂n) ds with fundamental solution log r
results.modern_name: Green's representation formula in the plane
results.usually_credited_to: Green 1828; in this planar form, Riemann 1851 (Dissertation Art. 10)

results.what: u(O_0) = (1/2π) ∫_0^{2π} u dφ on circles around O_0

deep.surprise_reason: This is essentially the text of Art. 10 of Riemann's published 1851 doctoral dissertation. The content (Green's identity, the representation formula, mean value, the removable-singularity argument) is well known and attributed to him in this form.

transcription_corrections: Line 1 begins 'aber sind von einander unabhängig.', the end of Art. 9. The transcription is consistent with the image.

In 'dass sie [-...-] sich von ersten Differentialquotienten' the struck word and the surrounding text are uncertain. The published dissertation reads approximately 'dass sie nebst ihren ersten Differentialquotienten etwaige Unstetigkeiten jedenfalls nicht längs einer Linie erleidet'. The manuscript should be rechecked here.
The final formula '-∫_0^{2π} u ∂log r/∂r r dφ - log r ∫ ∂u/∂p ds' matches the image. The trailing 'welcher' continues onto the next page ('Werth, wenn u im Punkte O_0 stetig ist ...').
